paper_metadata.title: Thermophysical and magnetic properties of Co-Ni-Mo-Al-Ta class of tungsten free Co-based superalloys

evidence.quote: Cobalt-based superalloys strengthened by precipitation of the ordered γ′-phase is extensively investigated in recent times.
the thermal and magnetic properties of Ta/Mo stabilized superalloys of compositions Co-30Ni-10Al-5Mo-2Ta-xTi-yCr (x = 0, 2; and y = 0, 2, 5, 10 at%)
Table 1 Nominal and measured compositions (in at%) of the experimental alloys along with their designations.
30 g of each alloy was prepared by melting constituent elements (4 N purity) 8–10 times in a vacuum electric arc furnace equipped with a non-consumable tungsten electrode.
Following arc melting, the buttons were cast in rods and slabs using a suction casting unit equipped with water-cooled split copper molds.
The cast samples were given solution treatment by isothermally holding at 1250 °C for 25 h under 10−5 mbar vacuum level followed by water quenching.
The solutionized samples were aged at 900 °C for 50 h under vacuum (~10−5 mbar) and were subsequently furnace cooled.

The γ′ precipitates in the 30Ni2Ta alloy (Fig. 1(a)) are well distributed in the γ matrix.
The addition of the 2 at%Ti to 30Ni2Ta alloy increases the primary cuboidal shape γ′ volume fraction from 50 ± 3 to 62 ± 2 (%) with no evidence of secondary γ′ precipitates in γ channel.
Cr addition to 30Ni2Ta2Ti alloy changes the morphology from cuboidal to intermediate ellipsoidal shape and finally spheroidal shape for alloy Cr-10 as shown in Fig. 1(e).
The Ms of 43 emu/g and 30 emu/g were obtained in the Cr-free samples denoted as 30Ni2Ta and 30Ni2Ta2Ti.

The alloy with 2 at% Ti yields the highest Curie temperature of 713 °C while the base alloy denoted as 30Ni2Ta shows a Curie temperature of 718 °C.

Alloy with 2 at% Cr exhibits a lesser value of 513 °C compared to the two Cr-free samples.
The room temperature electrical resistivity of the alloys lies in the range of 95–130 µΩ-cm.
